title: How the early Ohio bands traveled
summary: Bands went by traction car or jalopy across Ohio, Indiana and as far as Pittsburgh; Columbus was strong on jazz.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: How did you -- how did the groups get around? You said that -- Ohio and Springfield --
In cars and -- in automobiles, surely.
They would travel down to Springfield.

Yes, they'd travel, surely. They traveled. Then we had the electric cars between Springfield, Columbus, Cincinnati and Dayton. One car propelled -- they called them traction cars. But most of the bands would buy an old jalopy and -- a couple of them and carried them around in their own car. And one car would hold -- as I say, there was only about four pieces, but if you had drums to bring along and music, they'd maybe do it in two cars. But these bands traveled all over Ohio and Indiana and even as far east as Pittsburgh. Yeah. Columbus was very smart on jazz in those days -- it was sharp.
